customFields: Extra fields for contacts, companies and campaigns, such as company size or acquisition channel. They sit next to the standard fields and show up on the record card.
machineLearning: The machine learning module scores contacts: who is likely to respond to a message (uplift) and how much a customer is expected to bring (expected value). It is off by default. Once it is on, a scoring run lets the priority list and campaign targeting use those scores.
modelRegistry: The models the scoring service can run: where their data comes from, their metrics, and the version in use now. Sync models re-reads the registry from the service.
provenance: Where the model got its training data: a public dataset, semi-synthetic demo data, or a demo model. A demo model shows how this works and is not proof of a real effect.
upliftScore: Uplift is how much more likely a person is to act because of your message. A high score means the person is likely to respond to the email but would not have acted without it. People who would buy anyway do not add uplift.
expectedValue: Expected customer value (CLV) is how much a customer is expected to bring over the next months. It is a forecast, not a guarantee.
priorityMode: The list can rank two ways. RFM ranks by recency, frequency and order value, with no machine learning. ML ranks by uplift and CLV model scores. If ML is on but its models or scores are not ready yet, the list falls back to RFM for now.
priorityCounts: The daily list holds up to 100 contacts per owner, the highest by priority, so a segment can contain more contacts than you see here. The number next to a segment shows how many of its contacts are on today's list and how many exist in the organization.
modelHonestNote: An estimate of a demo model on semi-synthetic data. It shows that the pipeline works and is not proof of a real effect; an individual treatment effect is never observed.
currency: Amounts are in your organization's currency ({currency}). An administrator can change it under Settings > Organization.
scores: Model scores for this contact: uplift (how likely a response to a message is) and expected value (how much the customer is expected to bring). They are a demo model forecast, not proof of an effect.
telegram: Connecting sends the same notifications to a Telegram chat and gives the bot a /today command with the contact list for the day. It is optional; in-app notifications stay on.
pipelineStageColor: A stage color is stored once and shown in both themes, so a custom shade can look different or get lost: a very dark one disappears on the dark background, a very light one on the light background. Check both previews under the field and prefer mid tones. The text color on the stage is chosen automatically.
pipelineProbability: Win probability is the chance that a deal in this stage will be won. The weighted pipeline value is the sum of open deal amounts multiplied by this probability.

segmentHint.leadMl: Who this contact is: what the model expects, and how they buy.
segmentHint.leadRfm: How this contact buys, compared with your other buyers.

model.persuadable: Contacting raises the chance of a response by {points} pp or more.
model.persuadableNoRules: Contacting clearly raises the chance of a response.
model.sureThing: Likely to buy without a message ({chance} or more), so a message adds little.
model.sureThingNoRules: Likely to buy without a message, so a message adds little.
model.doNotDisturb: Contacting may lower the chance. Kept at the bottom of the list.

rfm.champions: Bought recently, often and for a lot.
rfm.promising: Bought recently, but only once or twice.
rfm.needsAttention: Average on recency and frequency, may slip away.
rfm.atRisk: Used to buy often, but not lately.
rfm.hibernating: Few orders, none lately, but spent a fair amount.
rfm.lost: Has not ordered for the longest time.
rfm.regular: A buyer who fits none of the groups above.

segmentHint.rfmNote: Buying pattern compares the contact with your other buyers over 365 days.
segmentHint.modelNote: The model's estimate is from a demo model, not a measured effect.
segmentHint.leadModel: What the model expects when this contact is approached.

reasonsHint.lead: Why this contact is on today's list. A contact can have several reasons.
reasonsHint.upliftHigh: The model expects a response: uplift of {threshold} pp or more.
reasonsHint.taskDue: An open task for this contact is due now or overdue.
reasonsHint.dealStale: An open deal has not moved for {days} days.
reasonsHint.highValue: In the top 20 % of buyers by spend over 365 days.
reasonsHint.recentOrder: In the top 20 % of buyers by latest order.
reasonsHint.doNotDisturb: The model advises against contacting now.
reasonsHint.note: No reason shown means the contact is ranked by segment and score only.

upliftHint.lead: How much contacting this person changes the chance of a response, in percentage points (pp).
upliftHint.example: For example, +10 pp turns a 20 % chance into 30 %.
upliftHint.sign: Positive: contacting helps. Negative: contacting may hurt.
upliftHint.click: Click a value to see this person's own chances.
upliftHint.sureThing: when the chance without contact is {chance} or more
upliftHint.doNotDisturbNoRules: when the model expects contact to lower the chance
upliftHint.note: A demo model's estimate, not a measured effect.

nextStepHint.lead: What to do with this contact next. The first rule that applies wins.
nextStepHint.reviewDeal: An open deal has not moved for {days} days. Open the contact and move it forward or close it.
nextStepHint.call: An open task for this contact is due or overdue. Open the row to see the task, then call or write.
nextStepHint.winBack: At risk, hibernating or lost. Reach out with a check-in or an offer.
nextStepHint.reward: Champions and loyal customers. Thank them or offer a perk.
nextStepHint.nurture: Everyone else. Keep in touch with a short message.
nextStepHint.hold: The model says contacting now may lower the chance. Leave this person alone.

holdout.lead: The holdout, also called the control group, is a random part of the audience that deliberately gets no email.

holdout.text: Gets nothing, so it shows what people do without the email.

holdout.after1: Comparing the two shows what the email changed, not what would have happened anyway.
holdout.note1: The split is random and fixed when you prepare the campaign. A bigger holdout is more reliable but reaches fewer people now.

holdoutSize.lead: How much of the audience stays out of the email.

smaller.text: More people get the email, but only large differences can be noticed.

larger.text: A more reliable result, but fewer people get the email now.

holdoutSize.note1: The panel on the right shows both group sizes and the smallest difference this size can detect.

mde.lead: The smallest difference in conversion this campaign can reliably notice.
mde.intro1: A small holdout only notices large differences. If the real effect is smaller, the result will look like no effect.
mde.note1: Before the audience is frozen this assumes a 20 % baseline conversion. After that it uses the real group sizes.

srm.lead: A check that the email group and the holdout have the sizes that were planned.

alarm.text: The sizes differ more than chance explains. The comparison is not reliable and no conclusion is drawn.

srm.note1: This usually means the audience changed while the campaign was prepared.

template.lead: The email this campaign sends: a subject and an HTML body.

variables.text: Filled in for each person when the email goes out, for example the first name.

preview.text: Shows the email with sample data. Nobody receives it.

test.text: From the campaign page you can send one copy to yourself.

template.note1: Changing a template later does not change emails that were already sent.

variables.lead: Variables are placeholders that are replaced with each person's data when the email is sent.

unsubscribe.text: Link that lets the person opt out of future emails.

variables.note1: Select a variable to insert it at the cursor. Unknown variables are rejected when you save.

segment.text: Contacts that match its filters, such as owner, country, tag or days since the last order.

everyone.text: All contacts that have an email.

audience.note1: The count is what matches right now. It is fixed when you prepare the campaign.
audience.note2: Contacts on the suppression list are left out of both groups.

targeting.lead: Which part of the audience is eligible for the email.

uplift.text: Only the contacts the model expects to respond most to the email. Needs a completed scoring run.

rfm.text: Only the most recent, frequent and valuable customers.

targeting.note1: The rule is applied the same way to the email group and the holdout, so the comparison stays fair.
targeting.note2: Contacts that are not targeted get no email and are left out of the results.

targeted.lead: Targeted means the contact passed the targeting rule you chose.

emailYes.text: Gets the email and is counted in the results.

emailNo.text: Gets no email and is left out of the results.

holdYes.text: Would have been emailed. Counted in the results.

targeted.note1: Only targeted people are compared, in both groups.

prepare.lead: Preparing locks in who is part of the campaign.

audience.text: The list of contacts is fixed at this moment.

groups.text: Each contact is put at random into the email group or the holdout.

targeting.text: If you target by scores, the scores and the model version are fixed too.

prepare.note1: Nothing is sent yet. You can review the counts, then start sending.

startSending.lead: What happens when you start sending.

who.text: Only targeted contacts of the email group. The holdout and everyone else get nothing.

unsub.text: People who unsubscribed or are on the suppression list are skipped.

once.text: Is emailed at most once, even if the server restarts in the middle.

after.text: Emails already sent cannot be recalled or stopped.

startSending.note1: Progress and results appear on this page.

status.lead: Where the campaign is in its life.

draft.text: Still being set up. You can change everything.

preparing.text: The audience and the split are being fixed.

ready.text: Prepared. Nothing has been sent yet.

completed.text: All emails are processed. Results keep updating until the attribution window closes.

failed.text: Preparing did not finish. Open the campaign and prepare again.

progress.lead: How far sending has got. Only the email group is listed, because the holdout is never sent anything.
progress.note1: Sent means handed to the mail server. It does not mean the person opened the email.

recipients.lead: Everyone in the frozen audience, with their group, whether the email went out, and what they did afterwards.
recipients.note1: Use the filters to look at one group, at targeted people only, at one send status or at converted people.

sendStatus.lead: Whether the email to this person went out.

claimed.text: A worker has picked this person up right now.

retry.text: A temporary problem. The system tries again.

failed.text: Could not be sent. Retries ran out or the problem is permanent.

suppressed.text: Not sent because the person unsubscribed or is on the suppression list.

unknown.text: The send was interrupted, so we cannot tell whether it went out. It is not retried, to avoid a double send.

demo.text: A historic demo campaign. No email was sent.

sendStatus.note1: The holdout has no send status, by design.

conversionColumn.lead: Whether the person bought after the campaign started. Any order counts, not only the product in the email.

converted.text: Placed at least one order within the attribution window. The date of the first order is shown.

pending.text: The results have not been calculated yet.

hidden.text: Your access does not include this contact.

conversionColumn.note1: Revenue is the value of the orders placed within the window. The window is shown under Results.

conversionRate.lead: Conversion is the share of people who placed an order within the attribution window.

converted.text: Of them, how many ordered within {days} days of the start of sending.

conversionRate.note1: Any order counts, not only orders for the product in the email.

difference.lead: The difference in conversion between the email group and the holdout, in percentage points (pp).
difference.intro1: For example, 12 % against 10 % is a difference of 2 pp.

positive.text: The email group converted more. The email is estimated to have helped.

zero.text: This data shows no sign that the email helped.

difference.note1: Read it together with the 95 % interval. It describes this campaign and does not by itself explain why.

interval.lead: The range the real difference most likely lies in (95 % interval).
interval.intro1: The groups are only samples of your audience, so the exact number is an estimate.

zero.text: The data cannot tell an effect from chance.

above.text: The data point to a real positive effect.

below.text: The data point to a real negative effect.

pValue.lead: How surprising this difference would be if the email had no effect at all.

small.text: Hard to explain by chance alone.

pValue.note1: It is not the probability that the email works.

revenueDifference.lead: The gap in average revenue between the two groups, multiplied by the size of the email group.
revenueDifference.note1: It describes the gap in this data, not a proven cause.

attributionWindow.lead: The period after sending when purchases count for this campaign.

length.text: {days} days from the start of sending.

open.text: The figures are provisional and can still change.

attributionWindow.note1: Purchases outside the window are not counted.

provisional.lead: Whether the figures can still change.

provisional.text: The attribution window is open. New purchases can still arrive.

provisional.note1: No conclusion is drawn from provisional figures.

simulated.lead: A demo campaign. Its orders and its effect were generated by a simulation.
simulated.note1: No real emails were sent and no real customers reacted. It shows what results look like.
